evidence_detail: 22 rows / 22 distinct InChIKeys independently reproduced from the three-gate intersection: |AI_CONSENSUS_ACCEPTED|=22, |v06_model_ready|=73, intersection=22, 0 accepted-but-not-ready, 0 accepted-and-excluded (build_candidate_pool_v2.py:79-85). Numeric outputs byte-identical across 2 reruns (candidate_pool_v2_draft.csv, candidate_exclusion_audit.csv, temperature_vocabulary_mapping.json). DEFECT D1: gate 3 is a no-op - ready & excluded = 0 rows, so 'three independent gates' is really two; the report line 'gate 3 n_passing = len(ready) = 73' (build_candidate_pool_v2.py:319) prints the gate-2 count under a gate-3 label, which cannot fail. DEFECT D2: the closed-interval temperature test (build_candidate_pool_v2.py:222-226) can never fail either - all 22 pool T_K values (293.15, 298, 298.15, 298.2, 300.15, 303.15) lie inside [293.15, 303.15], so n_pool_rows_outside=0 by construction and the rule tests nothing. DEFECT D3: b02_four_of_four is hardcoded to the string 'true' (build_candidate_pool_v2.py:102) instead of being derived from n_pass / consensus_status; the field is a constant, not evidence. No leakage: dielectric is carried through but never used as an admission filter, so admission is not label-circular. Held (not failed) because the pool membership and lineage are correct and reproducible; the defects are in the supporting audit claims, which overstate gate independence.

Recomputation from predictions_loo.csv MATCHES the as-delivered manifest exactly: X0 MAE 17.446507 / RMSE 20.931398 / bias -16.720897 / R2 -1.820290; X0+X1 MAE 17.286655 / RMSE 18.853363 / bias -17.009452 / R2 -1.288099; constant-baseline MAE 10.806223 (mean epsilon 17.315455). All five statistics agree to <5e-6 under an independent numpy re-solve. So arithmetic is not the problem - the model specification is. DEFECT D4 (fatal): ridge_loo (run_e1_structure_vs_electronic.py:139-150) standardises X but never centres y, so the fit is forced through the origin in standardised space. Predictions therefore collapse to a band around 0 (mean_pred 0.5946 against mean_true 17.3155) while true epsilon spans 1.93-44; the reported MAE is within 0.8% of the trivial 'always predict 0' baseline of 17.3155, and bias ~= -MAE is the signature of a missing intercept. Adding the intercept alone (identical features, identical lambda=1.0) gives X0 MAE 10.2435 (R2 -0.1110) and X0+X1 MAE 6.5044 (R2 +0.5397) - both now BEAT the 10.8062 constant baseline. The reported 'beats_constant_baseline=false' and the whole negative-result narrative therefore invert once the intercept is restored; the project's own E1b (bias_vs_ranking_diagnostic.abs_bias_over_mae = 1.0, diagnosis CALIBRATION_FAILURE_NOT_INFORMATION_FAILURE, debiased MAE 10.0012) confirms this independently. DEFECT D5: the permutation null shuffles y and refits (lines 252-261). For the question 'does this feature set explain variance' the correct null permutes the FEATURES and keeps y fixed; shuffling y destroys the X-y association and, with a no-intercept model, both the observation and the null are pinned to E|y|, so the test has almost no power to detect a real signal. Under a feature-permutation null the X0+X1 set reaches p(R2>=obs)=0.004 and p(MAE<=obs)=0.036 - i.e. the opposite reading. DEFECT D6: one RNG stream (random.seed at line 215) is shared across both models inside the loop, so each model's p-value depends on loop order; re-seeding per model moves X0+X1 from p=0.060 to p=0.042, straddling the 0.05 threshold the report quotes (0.164/0.060 at line 362 of e1_report.md). Seed sweep gives X0+X1 p in [0.034, 0.069]. DEFECT D7: there is no null at all for the Delta-MAE quantity the report reasons over (section 4 of e1_report.md, lines 366-379); an added permutation of the delta gives p_two_sided=0.824, i.e. the -0.159852 delta is pure noise. DEFECT D8: dead variables - y_all (line 190) is computed and never used; r2s (line 254) is filled and sorted but never read; statistics (line 44) is imported and never used. No leakage: lambda is fixed a priori at 1.0 (never tuned on the test fold) and _standardise is fitted on the training fold only (lines 146-148), verified at runtime (train-fold mean 7.619048 vs all-data 7.636364). FAIL because the headline conclusion is an artefact of the missing intercept, not a property of the descriptors.

The identical-fingerprint claim VERIFIES: with an independent RDKit Morgan r=2/2048-bit computation over all 231 pairs, exactly 2 pairs reach Tanimoto 1.0 - octanedinitrile/heptanedinitrile and nonane/heptane - touching 4 molecules, matching the delivered structural_distance_ood.csv rows EPSV04-R008/R012/R034/R045 (nn_tanimoto=1.0) and the manifest count of 4. Published abs_error values reproduce exactly (22.5762, 16.6064, 16.8593, 21.8746; all match to <5e-4). Leakage check PASSES: run_e4_domain_generalization.py:313-318 builds tr as [j for j in range(n) if j != i] and predicts mols[i], so no molecule trains on itself; leave-one-family-out arithmetic is exact (n_train + test_n = 22 on every measured row) and the family is removed wholesale. BUT the INTERPRETATION attached to those 4 rows is wrong. The report (e4_report.md section 7, mirrored in model_boundary_report.md) asserts the identical-fingerprint error is 'pure descriptor blindness' that 'cannot be fixed by more data'. Two independent refutations: (a) the error is almost entirely the missing-intercept extrapolation blow-up - with an intercept the same 4 rows fall to MAE 2.79 (max 5.15) from 19.48 (max 22.58); (b) the premiss 'the descriptors cannot distinguish them' is false - the feature vectors are NOT identical (nonane vs heptane molecular_volume_A3 162.048 vs 128.656; octanedinitrile vs heptanedinitrile 147.784 vs 131.408), only the 2048-bit fingerprint collides, and the y difference is 3.77 for the dinitrile pair. The report's own E1b manifest already flags this as 'needs restatement'. DEFECT D9: no Tanimoto/size caveat - the 'unclassified' family (4 of 22 molecules) contains sulfolane, a sulfone that simply has no SMARTS rule in FAMILY_RULES (run_e4_domain_generalization.py:68-82), and the comment 'most specific wins' is misleading because 13 of 22 molecules match several rules (e.g. dimethyl carbonate matches carbonate, ester and ether) and the first-match order is arbitrary. DEFECT D10: def rank() and the Spearman block (lines 363-381) are recomputed on rounded 4-dp values from dist_rows rather than raw errors, and statistics (line 52) is imported but unused. Held rather than failed because the fingerprint arithmetic and the leakage discipline are sound and reproducible; the defect is the causal story built on top.

Top-k recomputation MATCHES: n=22, k=max(1,ceil(22/10))=3, oracle mean 37.83, model mean 24.45, pool mean 17.3155, regret 13.38, regret/headroom 0.6522, overlap 1/3, Spearman(pred,true)=+0.7549, and P(random>=model)=0.16 (independent 2000-draw resample reproduces 0.16; 20000 draws give 0.154). The frozen-k and predefined-baseline rules are genuinely respected and no lambda tuning occurs, so no leakage. DEFECT D11 (fatal): the noise-ladder inference is an artefact. The RNG IS consistently seeded - random.Random(SEED) is rebuilt inside the sigma loop (run_e6_screening_decisions.py:274), so every sigma draws the SAME uniform stream; the monotone regret decrease is therefore NOT a re-drawing artefact, and I reproduce the exact published ladder (13.38, 13.38, 13.38, 12.8983, 10.933, 10.5613). The defect is the opposite one: the ladder is a RETURN TO THE MEAN, not evidence that 'noise undoes a bias'. Regret is a concave function of sigma with an interior minimum near sigma~6 (regret 10.23 at sigma=6, then 10.35 at 8, 10.89 at 10, 11.53 at 12, 12.78 at 16, 14.66 at 24, 15.85 at 32), and as sigma->infinity it tends back to the uniform-random regret of 20.5145 - i.e. the model at sigma=0 (13.38) is already BETTER than random, not worse. The script only samples sigma in [0,8], stopping on the descending branch, and then reads a local decrease as a monotone global anti-correlation. DEFECT D12: the decision rule at run_e6_screening_decisions.py:302-306 tests 'is regret at sigma=8 lower than at sigma=0' and labels the result REGRET_DECOUPLED_AND_ANTI_CORRELATED; the label 'anti-correlated' is unsupported - Spearman is +0.7549 (POSITIVE), so the model ranks correctly, it is merely biased low. DEFECT D13: the ladder's MAE is computed against the NOISY predictions (trial_maes at lines 281-282) rather than the un-noised model, so 'MAE rises while regret falls' compares a corrupted predictor's error to a rank statistic of the same corruption; the honest comparison is bias-corrected MAE vs regret. DEFECT D14: regret_monotone_down (line 302) uses a <= tolerance over the sampled grid only, so it can be 'true' purely because the grid never crosses the minimum - a check that cannot detect its own counterexample. Also unused: mae_span/regret_span feed only a COUPLED branch (line 337) that is unreachable given the ordering of the if/elif, and the E6 feature list silently drops total_energy_hartree relative to E1's X1 (11 vs 12 columns) with no note. FAIL because the H3 'supported and worse than expected' conclusion is an artefact of sampling only one branch of a concave curve.

Systemic defects, independent of the per-experiment rows. S1 (fatal, shared estimator): the identical no-intercept ridge is copy-pasted into E1 (run_e1_structure_vs_electronic.py:139-150), E4 (run_e4_domain_generalization.py:163-172), E6 (run_e6_screening_decisions.py:130-140) and E1b, so every reported MAE / R2 / bias / regret in B05 is computed against a model that cannot reach the label mean. Three separate experiment reports build a 'the descriptors have no information' narrative on top of this single coding error, and the project's own E1b manifest already records the correct diagnosis (abs_bias_over_mae = 1.0, CALIBRATION_FAILURE_NOT_INFORMATION_FAILURE) while E1/E4/model_boundary_report.md contain ZERO references to E1b, intercept, calibration, bias or de-biasing - verified by grep. The gate (outputs/b05/b05_gate_status.json) is 'gate_open: true' despite this. S2 (reproducibility): I ran the full B04+B05 chain twice from identical inputs. All 14 numeric CSV outputs are byte-identical; 11 files differ, and every difference is confined to generated_at_utc timestamps and the doc-hash fields derived from them (verified by diffing with timestamp lines filtered out - zero residual differences). So the pipeline is deterministic in its numbers but NOT byte-reproducible as a file set; manifests cannot be used as a content-addressed integrity check, because e1_manifest.json, e4_manifest.json, e6_manifest.json and b05_gate_status.json each embed a SHA-256 over a report that contains its own timestamp. S3 (provenance drift): while this review was running, all five B05 scripts were rewritten in place (run_e1*.py 462->499 lines, run_e4 702->714, run_e6 503->544, build_model_boundary_report 279->314) to add the missing intercept, and outputs/b05 was regenerated. My audited state is frozen at outputs/b04_b05_review/as_delivered/. Consequence: the delivered E1 metrics changed from MAE 17.4465/17.2867 with beats_constant_baseline=false to 10.2435/6.5044 with true, and E4's identical-fingerprint MAE fell from 19.48 to 2.79 - exactly the corrections my independent recomputation predicted. No script carries a version bump or changelog to distinguish the two states, and E1b (which triggered the rewrite) is still not wired into the gate. S4: feature_registry_v2.csv registers 11 features and is certified as the traceability spine, but E1 actually fits 12 (it adds total_energy_hartree, unregistered), while E4/E6 fit 11 without it - so the same nominal 'X1 electronic' tier means different things in different experiments and the registry cannot reproduce E1's n_features=12. S5: polarizability_au and polarizability_A3 are an exact scalar multiple (ratio 0.1481847374-0.1481847517, Pearson r = 0.9999999999999951), so X1 carries one redundant column that inflates p and destabilises the ridge with n=22. S6: model_boundary_report.md is presented as 'mechanically generated from the manifests so it cannot drift from the numbers' (build_model_boundary_report.py:56) yet hardcodes narrative claims - family MAE range '12.8-21.3' (line 205), 'MAE only drops 0.16' (line 207) and the H2/H3 verdicts - none of which are derived from the manifest values, so the no-drift guarantee is false for exactly the sentences that carry the scientific conclusion. S7: build_model_boundary_report.py:234 hardcodes required_deliverables['model_boundary_report.md']=True instead of testing the path, a check that can never fail.
